title: Campus life 1: courses & academics
description: Vocabulario académico de universidad norteamericana que aparece constantemente en las conversaciones del TOEFL.

cards.definition: The process of officially signing up for courses each term.
cards.example: Registration for the spring semester opens on Monday, so I need to pick my courses this weekend.

cards.definition: The document listing a course's topics, readings, assignments and grading.
cards.es: programa / guía docente de la asignatura
cards.example: According to the syllabus, the research paper is worth 40% of the final grade.

cards.definition: Set times when a professor is available in their office to meet students.
cards.example: If you're confused about the assignment, come to my office hours on Thursday afternoon.

cards.definition: A course you must pass before you can take another one.
cards.example: Introduction to Statistics is a prerequisite for this research methods class.

cards.definition: A graduate student who helps teach a course, leads discussion sections and grades work.
cards.example: The TA will return your lab reports during Friday's discussion section.

cards.definition: University teachers of different ranks.
cards.example: My instructor for this course is an adjunct who also works at a law firm.

cards.definition: A talk given by a professor to a large class.
cards.example: The lecture hall was packed for the first biology lecture of the year.

cards.definition: A small class focused on discussion.
cards.example: Participation in the weekly discussion section counts for 15% of the grade.

cards.definition: The unit used to measure course load toward a degree.
cards.example: I need twelve credits to be a full-time student this semester.

cards.definition: Your main / secondary field of study.
cards.example: She's majoring in economics with a minor in environmental studies.

cards.definition: A course you choose freely, not required for your major.
cards.example: I took film history as an elective, and it turned out to be my favorite class.

cards.definition: A course everyone in a program must take.
cards.example: Writing 101 is a core requirement for all first-year students.

cards.definition: To attend a course without receiving a grade or credit.
cards.example: I'm auditing the philosophy class because I'm interested but don't need the credits.

cards.definition: To withdraw from / join a course early in the term.
cards.es: darse de baja / alta de una asignatura
cards.example: The drop/add period ends Friday, so if you want to switch sections, do it now.

cards.definition: The official record of a student's courses and grades.
cards.example: Graduate schools will ask for an official transcript from every university you attended.

cards.definition: The average of a student's grades on a 0–4 scale.
cards.example: You need a GPA of at least 3.0 to keep the scholarship.

cards.definition: A temporary grade allowing a student to finish work after the term.
cards.example: After her surgery, the professor gave her an incomplete so she could finish the project in summer.

cards.definition: Extra time to submit an assignment.
cards.example: I emailed my professor to ask for a two-day extension on the essay.

cards.definition: Exams held in the middle / at the end of the term.
cards.example: The midterm covers chapters one to six, and the final is cumulative.

cards.definition: A written account of a laboratory experiment.
cards.example: Each lab report must include your hypothesis, method, results and discussion.

cards.definition: A long written assignment, often with research.
cards.example: My term paper on urban heat islands is due the last week of classes.
cards.warning: 'paper' aquí NO es 'papel', sino un trabajo o artículo.

cards.definition: The professor who supervises a student's thesis.
cards.example: My thesis advisor suggested narrowing my topic to a single region.
cards.note: 'academic advisor' = orientador que ayuda a elegir asignaturas.

cards.definition: A long piece of original research for a degree.
cards.example: She is writing her senior thesis on the history of public libraries.
cards.note: US: 'dissertation' suele ser la tesis doctoral y 'thesis' el trabajo de grado o máster; en UK es casi al revés ('dissertation' = TFG/TFM, 'thesis' = tesis doctoral).

cards.definition: Using someone else's work without credit / the rules about honesty.
cards.example: Copying from a website without citing it is considered plagiarism and violates the academic integrity policy.

cards.definition: To give the source of a quote or idea.
cards.example: Make sure you cite at least five peer-reviewed sources.

cards.definition: Texts students must read for a course.
cards.example: I'm behind on the assigned reading, so I'll spend the weekend in the library.

cards.definition: To adjust grades relative to how the whole class performed.
cards.es: calificar en función de la media del grupo
cards.example: The exam was so difficult that the professor decided to grade it on a curve.

cards.definition: A grading option with no letter grade.
cards.example: I'm taking the dance class pass/fail so it won't affect my GPA.

cards.definition: Divisions of the academic year.
cards.example: This semester I'm taking four courses and working part-time.

cards.definition: First-, second-, third- and fourth-year undergraduates (US).
cards.example: As a sophomore, you can't register for senior-level seminars yet.

title: Campus life 2: services & student life
titleEs: Vida universitaria 2: servicios y vida estudiantil
description: Alojamiento, dinero, servicios y vida en el campus: el contexto típico de Listen to a Conversation y Daily Life.

cards.definition: A university building where students live.
cards.example: First-year students are required to live in a dorm on campus.
cards.note: 'dorm' es informal; los avisos oficiales dicen 'residence hall'.

cards.definition: A student employed to supervise and help residents of a dorm floor.
cards.es: estudiante responsable de planta en la residencia
cards.example: If the heating breaks, report it to your RA first.

cards.definition: A person you share a room or apartment with.
cards.example: My roommate and I agreed on quiet hours after 11pm.

cards.definition: A prepaid package of meals at campus dining halls.
cards.example: I switched to a smaller meal plan because I cook most dinners myself.
collocations: sign up for a meal plan

cards.definition: The place where students eat on campus.
cards.example: The dining hall extends its hours during final exams week.

cards.definition: The money paid for teaching / other university costs.
cards.example: Tuition went up by 4% this year, and there's a new technology fee.

cards.definition: Money given or lent to students to help pay for university.
cards.example: You should visit the financial aid office if your family's situation has changed.

cards.definition: Money for study that does not have to be repaid.
cards.example: She received a scholarship that covers half of her tuition.

cards.definition: A part-time campus job funded as part of financial aid.
cards.es: trabajo en el campus financiado por la ayuda al estudio
cards.example: My work-study job at the library desk is only ten hours a week.

cards.definition: The office managing enrollment, records and transcripts.
cards.example: The registrar's office can tell you whether your transfer credits were accepted.

cards.definition: The office that handles student payments and bills.
cards.example: There's a hold on my account until I pay the bursar's office.

cards.definition: A block that prevents registration until a problem is solved.
cards.example: I can't register because there's a hold on my account for an unpaid library fine.

cards.definition: The identification card for students.
cards.example: You'll need your student ID to enter the gym and borrow books.

cards.definition: To borrow / extend the loan of / late to return (library books).
cards.es: sacar en préstamo / renovar / con retraso
cards.example: You can renew the book online unless someone has placed a hold on it; overdue books incur a fine.

cards.definition: Library material kept for short loans for a specific course.
cards.example: The professor put two copies of the textbook on reserve at the library.

cards.definition: Students who meet to study together.
cards.example: Joining a study group really helped me prepare for the chemistry final.

cards.definition: A campus service offering free help with writing or subjects.
cards.es: centro de apoyo a la escritura / tutorías
cards.example: Before you submit the essay, take it to the writing center for feedback.

cards.definition: Campus services for mental and physical health.
cards.es: servicio de orientación psicológica / centro de salud
cards.example: The counseling center offers free stress-management workshops during exam season.

cards.definition: Office that helps with jobs and internships / an event with employers.
cards.es: servicio de empleo / feria de empleo
cards.example: Career services can review your résumé before the career fair next month.

cards.definition: A temporary work placement for students.
cards.example: I'm hoping to get a summer internship at an environmental consulting firm.

cards.definition: Activities outside the academic program, like clubs and sports.
cards.example: Employers often value extracurricular activities that show leadership.

cards.definition: A building with student services, food and events; also the student government.
cards.es: centro de estudiantes / sindicato de estudiantes
cards.example: The bookstore is on the ground floor of the student union.

cards.definition: Introductory events for new students.
cards.example: During orientation week, new students take a campus tour and meet their advisors.

cards.definition: A free bus that runs around the campus and nearby areas.
cards.example: The campus shuttle runs every fifteen minutes until midnight.

cards.definition: Official permission to park in campus lots.
cards.example: Commuter students must buy a parking permit to use the north lot.

cards.definition: Accommodation outside university property.
cards.example: Many juniors move into off-campus housing because it's cheaper.

cards.definition: A rental contract / money paid in advance as protection for the landlord.
cards.example: Read the lease carefully: you might lose your security deposit if you leave early.

cards.definition: The last time by which something must be done.
cards.example: The deadline for scholarship applications has been extended to March 15.

cards.definition: A board for posting announcements / an announcement.
cards.example: I saw a notice on the bulletin board about a volunteer program.

cards.definition: The ceremony where degrees are awarded.
cards.example: Commencement will be held outdoors unless it rains.
